initial.chief_complaint: Acute interscapular pain followed by progressive bilateral leg weakness and bowel/bladder incontinence.

provider_metadata.assistant_note: Sudden interscapular pain followed by paraparesis and sphincter dysfunction suggests acute spinal cord compression or a vascular cord injury (spinal epidural hematoma, spinal cord infarction or aortic dissection). I'm checking vital signs first to assess stability and look for signs of dissection.

facts.value: Alert, GCS 15; leg strength 0/5, arm strength 5/5, absent perianal sensation, preserved bulbocavernosus reflex.
Vital signs described as stable; no numerical values reported.

args.urgency: immediate (post-operative transfer from the operating room)
args.rationale: 23-year-old man with a spontaneous C6-T2 spinal epidural hematoma compressing the cord. It caused complete paraplegia (legs 0/5), perianal sensory loss and bowel/bladder incontinence. He has had an emergency laminotomy and hematoma evacuation. He needs close post-operative monitoring in the neuro-ICU for: serial neurological exams to catch a recurrent hematoma, blood pressure support to keep spinal cord blood flow adequate, and care of his neurogenic bladder and bowel. Several results are still pending. PT/INR and aPTT were not returned, so a coagulopathy has not been ruled out. The cause of the bleed is still unknown, including a possible vascular malformation or infection. His WBC is also raised at 13,000/µL.
args.followup_or_handoff: Hand off to neurosurgery and the neuro-ICU team. Orders: hourly neurological checks; urgent repeat MRI if his neurology gets worse; keep MAP at 85 mmHg or higher for 5-7 days; indwelling urinary catheter and a bowel regimen; mechanical DVT prophylaxis, delaying drug prophylaxis until neurosurgery clears it. Check PT/INR, aPTT and fibrinogen. Follow up the histopathology and culture results from the surgical specimen. If no cause is found, consider spinal angiography or contrast MRI to look for an epidural vascular malformation. Start pressure-injury prevention. Refer early to physical therapy, occupational therapy and spinal cord injury rehabilitation.
